conviction_note: The Q3 numbers are not pre-released, but GEA has a fixed habit of filing an Ad-hoc against VARA consensus when a quarter deviates materially (Oct 2024, Jul 2025, Jan 2026, Jul 2026), and none has been filed for Q3 by 6 Nov. So the release is most likely in line and the guide unchanged, which points to a moderate move (abs 3.5, above the 2.3% reiterated-guide median because the numbers are new and this name fell 2.0% and 4.9% on its last two scheduled releases without an ad-hoc). The findings offset to 0.0: a conservative implied H2 guide and a record Alfa Laval quarter pull one way, JBT Marel's CPG book-and-ship weakness, a tough Q4 order comparison and a name that sells scheduled beats pull the other. p_up is 47, a slight sell-the-news lean from a stock at its record high and at the consensus target.

findings.finding: GEA has filed no Ad-hoc on Q3 2026 by 6 Nov. It has a consistent practice of filing one when a quarter deviates from VARA consensus (Q3 2024 on 11 Oct 2024, Q2 2025 on 31 Jul 2025, FY2025 on 26 Jan 2026, Q2 2026 on 21 Jul 2026), so Q3 is most likely close to consensus. On the two recent scheduled releases with no Ad-hoc beforehand (6 Nov 2025, 11 May 2026), the stock fell about 2.0% and 4.9% despite 'strong quarter' headlines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ad-hoc beat days: +3.4% (26 Jan 2026), +5.65% (22 Jul 2026, the day after the after-hours Ad-hoc). Scheduled releases with no pre-release: Q3 2025 about -2.0%, Q1 2026 -4.89% (Yahoo closes 8 May 59.25 to 11 May 56.35).
findings.original_quote: Vorläufige Zahlen für das zweite Quartal 2026 übertreffen Markterwartung – Anhebung der Guidance für das Gesamtjahr ... (VARA-Konsensus: 233 Mio. €) (21.07.2026). Translation: 'Preliminary Q2 2026 figures exceed market expectation, FY guidance raised.' This is the precedent; the EQS archive lists no comparable Q3 2026 item through 4 Nov 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. A reader who knows the Ad-hoc habit would already expect an in-line print. But the stock sits at a record (about 69, record 69.95 on 4 Nov) after the pre-close call and broker target raises, which looks like positioning for a beat, not for an in-line quarter. If the market had fully absorbed 'no Ad-hoc, so no big beat', the October rally would have faded into the print. Instead it has held at the highs.
findings.independence: The reaction history comes from the Yahoo tape (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/G1A.DE?range=1y&interval=1d); the Ad-hoc pattern comes from the EQS archive. Both rest on GEA's own disclosure channel.

findings.finding: At the 5 Oct 2026 Q3 pre-close call GEA signalled strong Q3 orders, with large orders (above EUR 15m each) totalling a low three-digit EUR million amount against about EUR 64m in Q3 2025, and confirmed the raised FY guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock made a record (68.50 intraday, 6 Oct) on the call, and Oddo (77), Barclays (79) and LBBW (76) raised targets.
findings.original_quote: Die Indikationen lassen für das dritte Quartal erneut starke Aufträge erwarten. (Translation: 'The indications point to strong orders again in the third quarter.') The large-order figure ('niedriger dreistelliger Millionenbetrag') is snippet_only from ms-aktuell.de, which returns 403 to both curl and WebFetch.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the stock rallied to a record on it and has held there. This is filed near zero because the market has already been told.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide implies a conservative H2: H1 organic growth was 8.2% against a FY range of 6-8%, and the H1 margin of 16.8% needs only about 17.2-18.0% in H2. Analysts on the Q2 call called the guide conservative, and the CEO said 'it might look conservative', so a narrowing toward the upper half is possible in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises came by Ad-hoc and moved the stock +3.4% and +5.65%. On 6 Nov 2025 the guide was reiterated and the stock fell about 2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Sell-side models already sit above the guide midpoint (the FY revenue consensus of EUR 5.88bn moved up after Q2). A narrowing in the release would confirm that, not surprise it. A formal raise would have needed an Ad-hoc, and there is none.
findings.independence: H1 figures in GEA's 10 Aug release: https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/gea-second-quarter-figures-double-digit-growth-in-order-intake-and-revenue-with-significantly-higher-profitability/4e1c133d-024f-4fcc-ba43-043100fdf10c_en

findings.finding: Management warned on the Q2 call not to expect Q4 2026 order intake above Q4 2025, which included the Baladna mega-order. MWB Research repeated the point in October, so the forward order commentary in the release is likely to read soft year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order-driven worries were behind past scheduled-day falls (dpa-AFX 'Anleger sorgen sich um Auftragslage', historical). There is no clean measured case.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and two sources have flagged it. It is left small because a repeated warning moves little.

findings.finding: Peer Alfa Laval reported record Q3 2026 orders on 27 Oct (+36% reported, +33% organic, SEK 23.2bn), with Food & Pharma transactional demand 'strong', but guided Q4 demand 'somewhat lower'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured read-across on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy. Most of Alfa Laval's surge is energy and marine, not dairy or food processing, so the read-across to GEA is weak and GEA's price was flat after 27 Oct (68.4 to 69).

findings.finding: Peer and counterparty-adjacent JBT Marel missed its own Q3 2026 revenue expectations on weaker CPG book-and-ship business in prepared food and beverage, and refined its FY revenue guide downward on 'lower, near-term CPG-related volume expectations'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured read-across on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: GEA's stock did not react around 30 Oct (67.9 to 68.7). This is a proxy for GEA's Food & Healthcare Technologies transactional business only, net of farming and dairy processing, which drove GEA's Q2.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.26, mostly a mechanical short-squeeze term on a stale 0.51% single position) and the flat run-up (+0.9% 20d) say little. My net-zero findings and slight sell-the-news tilt cut mildly against the positive lean, which is why p_up is 47, not above 50.
language_note: The German Ad-hoc text (EQS _de) carries GEA's explicit VARA-consensus comparison, which establishes the pre-release habit. The English version carries the same content, so this is not unique.

German retail and financial portals (goldesel.de, ms-aktuell.de) carried the only reports of the 5 Oct Q3 pre-close call: strong Q3 orders, large orders in the low three-digit EUR millions, MWB's Q4 comparison warning. The English sources found nothing on the pre-close call.
A German Börsen-Zeitung hit on Q3 Solutions orders turned out to be from 2018 and was rejected on its date.
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move' (18 of 23 names): abs_move_pct raised from 3.0 to 3.5. The numbers are new, and the name's own scheduled moves of 2.0% and 4.9% exceed the 2.3% reiterated-guide median.

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' and the core's sells-beats row: the no-Ad-hoc finding rests on two scheduled-day reactions, so it was cut from -0.8 to -0.5, and p_up moved from 46 to 47, toward 50.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the pre-close order signal was cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
